judge_context: One script with a main() entry point, a function that turns a video into per-frame foreground measurements (background subtraction against the empty first frame / MOG model), and a separate function that locates takeoff and landing from that signal. Tunable thresholds are named constants with a short rationale; no leftover debug windows (cv2.imshow), frame dumps or prints to stdout besides concise status.

case_items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
case_items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
case_items.question: Does jump_analyzer.py check that the video opened, handle videos where no runner/jump is detected with a clear non-zero exit instead of a crash or fake output, and avoid detection thresholds that only fit the example video?

criteria.perfect: Validates argv / file opening (cap.isOpened()), exits non-zero with a clear message on unreadable input or when no jump is detected, and uses relative or adaptive thresholds (e.g. derived from the empty first frame / background model) rather than absolute pixel constants only.
criteria.accept: Normal path robust; one failure path (e.g. no motion detected) raises an uncaught exception or writes placeholder values.
criteria.bad: Assumes success everywhere: no check that the video opened, index errors on empty detections, or silently writes 0/0 or default frames.

case_items.name: Output contract honoured
case_items.question: Does jump_analyzer.py take the video path from argv[1] and write /app/output.toml with exactly the integer fields jump_takeoff_frame_number and jump_land_frame_number?

criteria.perfect: Reads argv[1], writes /app/output.toml containing exactly the two required integer fields with the exact names; frame numbering convention is stated/consistent.
criteria.accept: Required fields correct but extra keys are emitted (e.g. velocity) or the output path is relative to cwd.
criteria.bad: Wrong field names/types (strings, floats), output path not /app/output.toml, or input path hard-coded instead of argv[1].
